title: SLOs & Error Budgets
summary: Service Level Objectives define how reliable a service must be from the user view. Error budgets convert that into a measurable allowance for change velocity vs stability.

sections.title: SLI, SLO, SLA
paragraphs: SLI: measured indicator (availability, latency). SLO: target on that indicator. SLA: contractual consequences. Engineers manage SLOs; legal owns SLAs.
Choose SLIs that mirror user pain — successful requests / total, or fraction under latency threshold — not CPU idle.

sections.title: Error budgets
paragraphs: If SLO is 99.9% monthly availability, budget is 0.1% failure. Burn the budget with incidents or risky releases; when exhausted, freeze features and fix reliability.
Multi-window burn-rate alerts catch fast burns (pages) and slow burns (tickets).

sections.title: Setting targets
paragraphs: Tighter than dependencies is impossible long-term. Stack SLOs with dependency math. Leave margin.
Different user journeys may need different SLOs (checkout vs admin export).

sections.title: Culture
paragraphs: Error budgets only work if leadership honors them. Otherwise they become dashboards nobody follows.

deepDive.title: SLOs & Error Budgets — Operations
paragraphs: Operating SLOs & Error Budgets in production means defining SLIs before tuning knobs, knowing amplification costs, and rehearsing failure modes.
Prefer reversible changes, feature flags, and canaries. Measure p50/p99 and error rate under load that matches production skew.
bullets: Define capacity from the scarcest resource
Keep rollback cheaper than forward repair when possible

deepDive.title: SLOs & Error Budgets — Failure modes
paragraphs: Common failures around SLOs & Error Budgets include overload, partial dependency outages, and silent correctness bugs that pass happy-path tests.
Inject faults in staging: latency, loss, clock skew, and disk full. Verify alerts fire and degradation is intentional.

expert.title: SLOs & Error Budgets — Expert notes
paragraphs: At the expert level, SLOs & Error Budgets intersects multi-region consistency, cost envelopes, and organizational constraints (team ownership, on-call load).
Write down the non-goals. Many outages come from optimizing a metric that was never the product requirement.

practices: Alert on burn rate, not raw CPU
keyTakeaways: SLOs quantify reliability as a product feature
whyItMatters: Without SLOs, teams argue opinions. With them, reliability work gets prioritized rationally.
reflectionQuestions: What is the user-facing SLI for your most critical journey?
numbersToKnow: Know your p99 latency budget before adding hops
Peak load ≠ average load — plan headroom (often 2–3×)
Cross-region RTT is often ~50–150ms one way
